phase3_findings.description: The new read-only-sandbox arm is triggered by the listing's own refusal, which the same diff's SKILL.md says never selects that arm; the arm is unreachable on its stated condition and misses the read-only case it was specified for.
The arm asserts inline stand-in blocks that a run reaching it on its stated trigger never posted, while forbidding the on-disk copies - leaving the run with neither channel.
The universal 'That single invocation's own output carries every outcome' is contradicted by the refusal case its own next clause routes.

The absent-file discriminator keys on an exit status the prose never says how to observe, and which a worktree-isolated harness refuses outright (issue #1633) - policy without mechanism, failing badly in both directions.

The freshness comparand (the run-slug pointer) is itself one of the four listed paths and is the file the read-only arm removes; with it absent the comparison is vacuous and unrouted, so a same-slug prior-run leftover reads as this run's.
The read-only discharge is ordered after the re-entry instruction it is meant to suppress, so a read-only run re-enters Step 3.6 before reaching it.

'A diagnostic naming a listed path with a non-zero status is an absent file' is over-broad: ls -l also emits a path-naming diagnostic on a permission failure, so an existing file is re-produced via the expensive Step 3.6.
The mandated ls -l timestamp comparison cannot decide the same-minute case and fails open; a portable finer-granularity form is unavailable (GNU-only / BSD-only flags are barred).
The slug-unestablished branch has no arm for .prflow/tmp itself being absent; a directory has no producing step to re-enter.
A missing binary and a refusal collapse onto one indistinguishable report though their remedies are opposite.
The new mkdir has no failure arm, and a refused mkdir is arguably not the 'refused write' the read-only selector names.
'Before any re-entry' can be read as a per-re-entry obligation to re-list.
The changeset over-claims 'which pipeline steps left artifacts behind' relative to the four paths enumerated.
The audit-artifact limb restates, with a weaker criterion, what step-4-present-create.md's presentation gate already owns.
A producing-step re-entry resumes at draft rendering without reconciling the draft it may have invalidated.
Step 3.5's steelman has no dedicated covered artifact - it appends into the derivation file - so a skipped steelman leaves the listing unchanged.

test_first_gate.decision: no-automated-test: the fix delta is agent-executed instruction prose that enters a model's context as instruction, so the Phase 2.4 model-context route applies and a dry-trace does not discharge it
test_first_gate.command: subagent RED/GREEN micro-test with a no-guidance control, 12 runs over three scenarios
test_first_gate.evidence: Q1 refusal-with-no-output, Q2 permission-denied, Q3 read-only-arm-with-successful-listing. No-guidance control 3/3, 0/3, 3/3. RED (pre-fix text) 1/3, 0/3, 0/3 - reproducing both shipped defects verbatim, one rep stating 'non-zero status makes silence read as absent' and another 'permission-denied diagnostic naming the path is treated as absent per the rule'. GREEN (first fix) regressed Q3 to 1/3, BELOW the unaided control, because the negation 'never by the listing's output' was not binding; restructuring to lead with the observable predicate as its own sentence produced GREEN3 at 3/3 with converged reasoning. An intermediate variant that only appended a clause scored 1/3 and was discarded. Q1/Q2 label field stayed noisy in GREEN while the stated reasoning was correct 3/3, attributed to the three-token rubric not mapping onto a two-hop rule.
